source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: The kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is like{H1819} ten{H6235} virgins{H1330} who took{H3947} their lamps{H5216} and went out{H3318} to meet{H7125} a bridegroom{H2860} and a bride{H3618}.

one_way_hebrew: חתן וכלה — the fixed Hebrew pair of Jer 7:34; 16:9; 25:10; 33:11 (קול חתן וקול כלה, 'the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride') and of Joel 2:16, where the assembly is gathered as 'the bridegroom goes forth from his chamber and the bride out of her chuppah (וכלה מחפתה).' A Hebrew author writes the pair as one breath; read with v. 10's לחופה, the parable stages Joel 2:16's three terms — bridegroom, bride, chuppah — of which Greek keeps only the first.
נר (H5216) — the lamp of Prov 6:23 ('the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light') and Ps 119:105; the virgins' lamps burn or go out on their own oil (see v. 8).
greek_deviations: THE BRIDE STANDS IN THE TEXT: the virgins go out לקראת חתן וכלה — 'to meet a bridegroom AND A BRIDE.' Greek Matthew has the bridegroom only (εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου); the bride survives in a minority Greek-Latin-Syriac strand (Codex Bezae, Old Latin, Syriac add καὶ τῆς νύμφης). The Hebrew families carry her without hesitation: Howard's apparatus records NO variant here — all Shem Tov mss read חתן וכלה — and the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise reads 'to the bridegroom and the bride.' With the bride restored, the ten virgins are the escort of a full wedding procession, and v. 10's chuppah completes the scene.

The chapter opens עוד אמר יש״ו לתלמידיו — 'Again Yeshua said to his disciples' — the discourse-resumption formula that stitches the Olivet teaching together (as at 24:27, 37, 42); Greek has bare 'Then' (Τότε), and its future 'shall the kingdom be likened' is present in the Hebrew: the kingdom IS like.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ד (Perek 104) begins here.
No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse — חתן וכלה is uniform across the Shem Tov mss.

verses.translation: Five{H2568} of them were{H1961} lazy{H6102} fools{H3684}, and five{H2568} of them were diligent and wise{H2450}.

one_way_hebrew: עצל (H6102) — Proverbs' sluggard (Prov 6:6, 'go to the ant, thou sluggard'; 24:30-34, whose vineyard runs down while he sleeps); כסיל (H3684) — Proverbs' fool. The verse speaks Proverbs' own moral vocabulary.
זריזות — the rabbinic virtue of zerizut, promptness in a commandment; a native post-biblical Hebrew word (no Greek equivalent stands behind it).
greek_deviations: The Hebrew doubles each verdict: not merely 'foolish' but עצלות כסילות — 'LAZY fools' — and not merely 'wise' but זריזות וחכמות — 'DILIGENT and wise.' Greek has the bare pair μωραί/φρόνιμοι. The added pair names the cause: folly here is laziness, wisdom is promptness — and עצל (lazy) returns as the master's verdict on the buried-money servant (vv. 26, 30), binding the two parables with one word the Greek does not have in either.
translation_notes: זריזות has no biblical Strong's number; it is living rabbinic Hebrew for 'prompt, diligent.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:2): וחמש] והחמש A; the second מהן omitted in AG.

verses.translation: The five{H2568} fools{H3684} brought out{H3318} their lamps{H5216}, but did not bring out{H3318} oil{H8081} with them{H5973}.

one_way_hebrew: The Hebrew repeats one verb — הוציאו... ולא הוציאו ('they brought out... they did not bring out') — the lamps came out, the oil did not. Greek uses two unrelated verbs (λαβοῦσαι... οὐκ ἔλαβον is the same only in later harmonization); the Hebrew's single repeated root makes the omission itself the point.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:3): כסילות] הכסילות A, העצלות G ('the lazy ones'); the second הוציאו] הוציא A; the closing עמהן omitted in EF.

verses.translation: And the wise{H2450} brought out{H3318} oil{H8081} in their vessels{H3627} with{H5973} their lamps{H5216}.

one_way_hebrew: שמן בכליהן — oil carried in vessels alongside the lamp: the arrangement of the Sanctuary itself, where the pure oil for the light is commanded separately from the lampstand that burns it (Exod 27:20; Lev 24:2). The lamp is common property; the oil each one brings is her own — which is why in v. 9 it cannot be shared.
textual_notes: The verse stands whole in the Shem Tov text; the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew has no counterpart to v. 4 (its text runs from v. 3 to v. 5), so the two Hebrew families witness the verse independently of each other.

verses.translation: And the bridegroom{H2860} delayed{H4102}, and behold{H2009}, they all{H3605} lingered{H4102} and slept{H3462}.

one_way_hebrew: מתמהמה (H4102) — Hab 2:3's word: 'though it tarry (יתמהמה), wait for it.' The same verb carries 24:48 ('my master delays in coming'): the wicked servant and the drowsy virgins fail the same test, the test of Hab 2:3 — the vision that tarries.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew gives bridegroom and virgins the SAME verb: ויתמהמה החתן... כלן נתמהמהו — 'the bridegroom delayed... they all delayed.' Greek switches pictures ('while the bridegroom tarried, they all nodded and slept'); the Hebrew says the escort matched the groom's lateness with their own — everyone lingered, and sleep followed.
translation_notes: ונשנה — an anomalous form; the sense 'and slept' (ישן, H3462) is fixed by the variants (B וישנו 'and they slept', EF ותשנה, G ונשנן) and by the Greek. Howard renders '(slept)' in parentheses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:5): נתמהמהו] נתמהמו A; ונשנה] וישנו B, ותשנה EF, ונשנן G.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} at the half{H2677} of the night{H3915}, behold{H2009}, a voice{H6963} was heard{H8085}: Behold{H2009}, the bridegroom{H2860} comes{H935} — come out{H935} to meet{H7125} him.

one_way_hebrew: ויהי בחצי הלילה — the exact clause of Exod 12:29 ('And it came to pass at midnight, YHWH smote all the firstborn') and Ruth 3:8 ('And it came to pass at midnight... behold, a woman lay at his feet' — Boaz the redeemer waked at midnight). Midnight in Scripture is the hour of redemption and judgment arriving together; Greek μέσης δὲ νυκτός translates the clock and loses the citation.
קול נשמע — 'a voice was heard': Jer 31:15's formula (קול ברמה נשמע). Greek has 'a cry arose' (κραυγὴ γέγονεν).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:6): והנה קול] וקול A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} all{H3605} the virgins{H1330} came{H935} and trimmed{H3190} their lamps{H5216}.

one_way_hebrew: והטיבו נרותיהן — היטיב את הנרות is the Torah's technical term for the priest's dressing of the Sanctuary lamps: 'every morning, when he dresses the lamps (בהיטיבו את הנרת)' (Exod 30:7). The virgins at midnight perform the priest's morning service on their own lamps; the Hebrew reader hears the Tabernacle, the Greek ἐκόσμησαν ('adorned') hears housekeeping.
translation_notes: The scan reads הבתולות; the circulating transcription's הבתותלות is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:7): הבתולות] + ההן ABEFG ('those virgins').

verses.translation: And the foolish{H3684} virgins{H1330} said{H559} to the wise{H2450}: Give{H5414} us of your oil{H8081}, for our lamps{H5216} have gone out{H1846}.

one_way_hebrew: נדעכו (H1846, da'ak) — Scripture reserves this going-out for one lamp only: 'the lamp of the wicked shall be put out (נר רשעים ידעך)' (Prov 13:9; 20:20; 24:20; Job 18:5-6; 21:17). The foolish virgins' own words pass Proverbs' sentence on them — their lamp went out the way the lamp of the wicked goes out. Greek σβέννυνται ('are being quenched') is any flame; דעך is the verdict.
translation_notes: The scan reads שנרותינו ('for our lamps'); the circulating transcription's שלרותינו is a typo, corrected here.

verses.translation: And the wise{H2450} answered{H6030}, saying{H559}: Go{H1980} now{H4994} to the sellers{H4376} and buy{H7069} for yourselves, for there is not{H369} enough{H1767} in our oil{H8081} for us and for you. We fear{H3372} that it will run short{H2637} for us.

one_way_hebrew: אין די — the idiom of Isa 40:16 (אין די בער, 'not sufficient to burn' — said of Lebanon's wood for the fire); the same construction, here said of oil for the flame.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew adds the wise virgins' motive in their own mouth: נירא שיחסר לנו — 'we fear it will run short for us' — absent from the Greek's flat 'lest there be not enough.' The refusal is not stinginess but sober fear: oil that must burn through the night cannot be halved.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:9): שלנו] + לכו A; לכן] לכם BEFG; נירא] נראה EF; לנו] + ולכן A.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when{H834} they went{H1980} to buy{H7069}, the bridegroom{H2860} came{H935}; and the ready ones{H3559} entered{H935} with him{H5973} to the chuppah{H2646}, and the gate{H8179} was shut{H5462}.

one_way_hebrew: חופה (H2646) — Joel 2:16 (וכלה מחפתה) and Ps 19:6 ('as a bridegroom coming out of his chuppah'). With v. 1's חתן וכלה the parable now holds all three of Joel's wedding words — bridegroom, bride, chuppah — a triad no translator working back from the Greek (which lacks bride and chuppah alike) could reassemble by accident.
greek_deviations: Two words the Greek does not have: the wise enter לחופה — 'to the CHUPPAH,' the marriage canopy (Greek: εἰς τοὺς γάμους, 'to the wedding feast') — and what shuts is השער, 'the GATE' (Greek: ἡ θύρα, 'the door'). The gate answers 24:33, where the Son of Man is 'near, at the gates' (לשערים): the same gates at which he stands are the gates that close.

המוכנות — 'the READY ones' (H3559, kun): the very word of 24:44, 'be ready (נכונים), for you do not know the hour.' The Hebrew discourse is woven on this root — the ready virgins here, the kingdom prepared (המוכן) in v. 34, the fire prepared (מוכן) in v. 41; Greek breaks the thread with different words.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse.

verses.translation: And afterward{H310} the foolish{H3684} came{H935} and called{H7121} at the gate{H8179}, saying{H559}: Our master{H113}, open{H6605} to us.

greek_deviations: The foolish call at the GATE (לשער) — continuing v. 10's city-gate word where Greek has none — and address the bridegroom once, אדוננו ('our master'), where Greek doubles the cry (κύριε κύριε, 'Lord, Lord'). The Hebrew keeps the doubled cry for Greek Matthew 7:21-22's own scene; here the plea is a single knock at a shut gate.
translation_notes: ואח״כ — the ms abbreviates ואחר כך ('and afterward') with gershayim.

verses.translation: And he answered{H6030} them: In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you, I do not{H369} know{H3045} who{H4310} you{H859} are.

greek_deviations: The refusal is sharper than the Greek: not 'I know you not' but איני יודע מי אתן — 'I do not know WHO YOU ARE.' The shut gate is not a lapse of memory; the unrecognized have no identity to the bridegroom at all.
באמת — 'in TRUTH I say to you' (אמת, H571), where Greek has ἀμήν. The Hebrew text freely commands both forms (אמן at v. 40); a translator from the Greek's fixed ἀμήν would not produce the variation.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:12): להן] להם EF; לכם] לכן G.

verses.translation: And therefore{H3651} watch{H8104} yourselves, for you do not know{H3045} the day{H3117} and the hour{H8160} when the bridegroom{H2860} will come{H935}.

one_way_hebrew: השמרו לכם — the Torah's own reflexive warning formula (Deut 4:23, השמרו לכם פן תשכחו; Exod 19:12). Greek γρηγορεῖτε ('stay awake') is a different command; the Hebrew says guard yourselves.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew names whose day it is: 'you do not know the day and the hour שיבא החתן — WHEN THE BRIDEGROOM WILL COME.' The critical Greek text ends blankly ('ye know neither the day nor the hour'); the Byzantine mss patch in 'wherein the Son of man cometh.' The Hebrew stays inside the parable: it is the bridegroom's arrival the watchers cannot time — the moral of vv. 1-12, not an imported title.
translation_notes: The scan reads ועל כן as two words; the circulating transcription joins them (ועלכן), corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:13): שיבא החתן] שהחתן עתיד לבא A ('that the bridegroom is destined to come').

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Another{H312} likeness{H1825}. The kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is like{H1819} a man{H120} going{H1980} on a far{H7350} journey{H1870}, who called{H7121} his servants{H5650} and scattered{H6340} his money to them.

one_way_hebrew: בדרך רחוקה — the phrase of Num 9:10 ('if any of you be on a far journey' — the Pesach-sheni clause): the man far from home whose appointed observance still awaits him.
ויפזר — Ps 112:9's word for the righteous openhand: 'he has scattered (פזר), he has given to the poor.'

ממון — mamon, the native Aramaic-Hebrew money word (as in 'you cannot serve God and mammon,' Matt 6:24); in the Hebrew text it needs no explanation, in the Greek it survives only as a transliterated foreignism (μαμωνᾷ).
greek_deviations: The Hebrew opens with its own rubric — דמיון אחר, 'another likeness' — and names the subject: the KINGDOM OF HEAVEN is like a man going far away. Greek has only 'For it is as a man travelling,' leaving the kingdom to be inferred from v. 1.

ויפזר להם ממונו — he SCATTERED his money to them (פזר, H6340), the base reading; mss ABEFG read ויפקוד ('entrusted'), assimilating toward the Greek παρέδωκεν. Scattering is the bolder picture — and it is the master's own word in vv. 24 and 26 ('gather what I did not scatter'): the base text lets him do at the start exactly what he says of himself at the end.
translation_notes: The scan reads עוד; the circulating transcription's עיוד is a typo, corrected here.
ממון has no biblical Strong's number; it is the living post-biblical word for wealth.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ה (Perek 105) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (25:14): דומה] + היא A; אחר] א׳ A; ויפזר] ויפקוד ABEFG (Howard marks the reading with a query).

verses.translation: To one{H259} he gave{H5414} five{H2568} gold-pieces{H2091}, to the second{H8145} two{H8147} gold-pieces, and to the third{H7992} one{H259} — to each man{H376} as was fitting for him he gave{H5414} — and he went{H1980} on his way{H1870}.

one_way_hebrew: וילך לדרכו — Gen 32:2's clause exactly (ויעקב הלך לדרכו, 'and Jacob went on his way'); the Hebrew narrative formula for a departure that opens a story.
greek_deviations: The coins are זהובים — 'gold-pieces' (zehuvim), the everyday coin-name of medieval Hebrew — where Greek counts in τάλαντα, the vast accounting unit of the Greco-Roman world. Each text speaks its own economy natively.

כראוי לו — 'as was FITTING for him,' where Greek has 'according to his ability' (κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν). The Hebrew measures the gift by what suits the man, not by his capacity — and the same word returns in v. 29 (הראוי לו, 'what is due to him').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:15): לשני] ולשני ABEF; the second נתן omitted in AEFG; לו] לא EF.

verses.translation: And the one who received{H6901} the five{H2568} gold-pieces{H2091} went{H1980} and gained{H7304} five{H2568} others{H312}.

translation_notes: הרויח — 'gained, made profit': the commercial hiphil of רוח (H7304), rabbinic Hebrew's ordinary word for profit; the noun ריוח appears in v. 27. The scan reads והרויח; the circulating transcription's והריוח is a typo, corrected here.
המקבל — 'the receiver' (קבל, H6901, the late-biblical receiving verb, Esth 4:4; Ezra 8:30): the parable consistently calls the servants by what they received, not what they owned.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:16): זהובים] omit F; והרויח] וירוח A.

verses.translation: And likewise{H3644} the one who received{H6901} the two{H8147} went{H1980}, bought{H7069} and sold{H4376}, and gained{H7304} five{H2568} others{H312}.

greek_deviations: Two deviations in one clause. First, the Hebrew tells you HOW he traded: הלך קנה ומכר — 'he went, bought and sold' — the plain Hebrew merchant idiom, where Greek has the abstract 'gained' (ἐκέρδησεν). Second, the base text says he gained FIVE others — the same yield as the five-piece man — where Greek says two. The later mss repair toward the Greek (A reads שנים 'two,' E corrects to שנים above the line, F writes יותר 'more'), but the base reading stands: measured by faithfulness rather than arithmetic, the two-piece servant earned the same 'five' — and both hear the identical greeting in vv. 21 and 23.
translation_notes: The base text's 'five' sits in visible tension with v. 22, where this servant presents 'two others'; the mss' corrections show the scribes felt it. The reading is preserved as Howard prints it.
The scan reads אחרים; the circulating transcription's החרים is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:17): חמשה] שנים A, with a supralinear correction to שנים in E, and יותר F ('more') for חמשה אחרים — the later mss assimilate toward the Greek's 'gained two more'; קנה ומכר] קונה ומוכר BEFG; והרויח] שהרויח A.

verses.translation: And the one who received{H6901} the one{H259} went{H1980} and dug{H2658} in the earth{H776} and hid{H2934} his master's{H113} money.

one_way_hebrew: ויטמון... בארץ — Achan's verb and hiding-place: 'behold, they are hid in the earth (טמונים בארץ) in the midst of my tent' (Josh 7:21-22). Buried treasure in Scripture is the signature of the man who took what was entrusted out of circulation.

טמן with עצל — Prov 19:24 and 26:15: 'the sluggard buries (טמן) his hand in the dish.' The servant who buries the money is the servant the master will call עצל, 'sluggard' (v. 26): the Hebrew joins the two Proverbs words in one man; Greek (ὀκνηρέ, ἔκρυψεν) uses words with no such kinship.
textual_notes: The transcriber's footnote notes ממון as the common Aramaic-Hebrew money word (Syriac mamona).

verses.translation: And after{H310} many{H7227} days{H3117} the master{H113} of those{H1992} servants{H5650} came{H935} and sought{H1245} from them an account{H2808} of the money.

one_way_hebrew: ואחר ימים רבים — 'after many days,' the prophetic long-delay formula (Ezek 38:8, מימים רבים; cf. Hos 3:4-5): the master's absence is told in the prophets' idiom for the long exile before the reckoning.

חשבון (H2808) — Ecclesiastes' word for the reckoning sought out (Eccl 7:25, 27: 'to seek out wisdom and the reckoning'). Greek συναίρει λόγον ('settles accounts') is bookkeeping; חשבון is Qohelet's audit of a life.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:19): ואחר] ואחרי A; רבים omitted in F; אדון] האדון F; העבדים ההם] אלו העבדים G.

verses.translation: And the one who received{H6901} the five{H2568} gold-pieces{H2091} approached{H5066}; he said{H559} to him: My master{H113}, five gold-pieces you gave{H5414} me — and behold{H1887}, here are five{H2568} others{H312} which{H834} I gained{H7304}.

one_way_hebrew: והא לך — 'and behold, here it is for you': the rare particle הא (H1887) of Gen 47:23, 'behold, here is seed for you (הא לכם זרע), and ye shall sow the land' — Joseph handing out capital to be worked. The servant returns the master's grain-word with the harvest.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:20): המקבל] מקבל G; the first זהובים omitted in G; אמר] ויאמר ABEFG; חמשה] מחמשה A; נתת] נתתו G; רוחתי] הרוחתי A; לך] + עשרה A ('ten' — assimilating toward the Greek's ten talents).

verses.translation: And his master{H113} said{H559} to him: Truly{H551}, a good{H2896} and faithful{H539} servant{H5650} you are{H859}. Because{H3282} you were{H1961} faithful{H539} over a little{H4592}, I will set you{H7760} over{H5921} much{H7235}; enter{H935} into the joy{H8057} of your master{H113}.

one_way_hebrew: נאמן (H539) — the covenant word for the proven servant: 'my servant Moshe... is faithful (נאמן) in all my house' (Num 12:7). The master's greeting sets each servant in Moshe's category; Greek πιστός translates it.
אמנם and נאמן share one root (אמן): 'TRULY — a FAITHFUL servant.' The master's first word already contains his verdict; only Hebrew shows the pun.
translation_notes: ויען here is יַעַן (H3282), 'because' (as in Isa 3:16) — not 'and he answered.'
The scan reads בשמחת (construct, 'into the joy of your master'); the circulating transcription's בשמחה is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:21): במעט] במועט G.

verses.translation: And also{H1571} the one who received{H6901} the two{H8147} gold-pieces{H2091} approached{H5066} and said{H559}: My master{H113}, two gold-pieces you gave{H5414} me — and behold{H2009}, two{H8147} others{H312} which{H834} I have gained{H7304}.

translation_notes: The servant here presents 'two others,' though v. 17 credited him with gaining five; see the note there — the mss' corrections at v. 17 show the scribes wrestling with the same tension.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:22): וגם... ויאמר] ויען מקבל ה״ב ויאמר G; שנים¹] השנים ABEFG — Howard notes that after this word F has three garbled words and omits all else down to v. 24; הזהובים] omit A, זהו׳ B.

verses.translation: And his master{H113} said{H559} to him: Truly{H551}, a good{H2896} and faithful{H539} servant{H5650} you are{H859}; and since{H3588} you were{H1961} faithful{H539} over a little{H4592}, I will set you{H7760} over{H5921} much{H7235}; enter{H935} into the joy{H8057} of your master{H113}.

greek_deviations: The greeting is word-for-word the greeting of v. 21: the servant who was given two and the servant who was given five receive one identical verdict — the point the base text of v. 17 (both 'gained five') already made in numbers.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:23): Verse 23 is omitted in F (see the note on v. 22).

verses.translation: And the one who received{H6901} the one{H259} approached{H5066} and said{H559}: My master{H113}, I know{H3045} that you are fierce{H5794} and hard{H7186}, and you reap{H7114} what you did not sow{H2232} and gather{H622} what you did not scatter{H6340}.

one_way_hebrew: קצר / זרע / אסף / פזר — reap, sow, gather, scatter: the Hebrew agricultural tetrad (Ps 126:5, 'they that sow in tears shall reap in joy'; Ps 112:9, 'he scattered, he gave to the poor'). The servant's charge quotes back the master's own scattering of v. 14 — ויפזר — which only the Hebrew base text still contains.
greek_deviations: The accusation is doubled in the Hebrew: עז וקשה — 'FIERCE and hard' — where Greek has only 'hard' (σκληρός). עז is the word for a fierce-faced nation (Deut 28:50, גוי עז פנים); the idle servant paints his master as the invader of the covenant curses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:24): ויאמר] omit G.

verses.translation: And from fear{H3374} of you I went{H1980} and hid{H2934} your gold-piece{H2091} — and behold{H1887}, you have what is yours.

one_way_hebrew: והא לך שלך — 'here, take what is yours': the servant returns the deposit with the same הא-formula of v. 20, but empty-handed of increase. The Mishnah's judgment on exactly this speech is proverbial (Avot 5:10, 'what is mine is mine and what is yours is yours' — the middling measure some say is the measure of Sodom); the Hebrew ear hears a man hiding behind strict property.
ומיראתך — 'from FEAR of you' (יראה, H3374): the servant misdirects the fear of the LORD onto a caricature of the master. Fear that buries is not the fear that begins wisdom (Prov 9:10).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:25): the first שלך] + בארץ A ('in the earth').

verses.translation: And his master{H113} answered{H6030} and said{H559}: Evil{H7451} and lazy{H6102} servant{H5650}! Since you knew{H3045} that I reap{H7114} what I did not sow{H2232} and gather{H622} what I did not scatter{H6340} —

one_way_hebrew: עצל (H6102) — the master's verdict is Proverbs' 'sluggard,' the word already laid on the foolish virgins in v. 2 (עצלות): one Hebrew word carries the moral of both parables. Greek uses ὀκνηρέ here and nothing at all in v. 2 — the thread exists only in the Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:26): ויאמר] + לו ABEF; the second לא] לו EG.

verses.translation: therefore{H2063} you were{H1961} obligated{H2325} to give{H5414} my property{H5233} to the money-changer, and at my coming{H935} I would receive{H6901} what is mine with{H5973} profit{H7305}.

one_way_hebrew: שולחני — the mishnaic money-changer, named from his שולחן, his table; Greek τραπεζίτης is likewise named from τράπεζα, a table. Each language coins the banker from its own furniture — the Hebrew is not translating the Greek word but matching it trade for trade.

חייב — 'you were OBLIGATED': the rabbinic legal term for one under binding duty (from חוב, H2325, 'to owe,' Dan 1:10). The master speaks halakhic Hebrew: depositing idle capital was not advice but obligation.
נכסי (H5233) — the late-biblical wealth word of Eccl 5:18 and 6:2 and Josh 22:8; natural to a Hebrew author of this register.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:27): לשולחני] + שירוח בהם G (apparently 'that he might profit with them').

verses.translation: Therefore{H2063} take{H3947} from him the gold{H2091} and give it to the one who gained{H7304} the five{H2568} gold-pieces{H2091}.

greek_deviations: The coin goes 'to the one who GAINED the five' (לאשר רווח החמשה זהובים) — Greek says 'to him who HAS the ten talents.' The Hebrew rewards the act of gaining, not the size of the holding; and since in the base text both traders gained five (v. 17), the reward singles out faithfulness, not the larger portfolio. Ms A betrays the difference by inserting 'ten' back at v. 20.
translation_notes: וחנותו — an anomalous form in the base ms; mss ABEFG read ותנוהו ('give it'), which Howard's English follows ('and (give it) to the one...'). If the base form is from חנן (H2603), the sense is 'bestow it graciously' — either way the command is the same.
textual_notes: The scan reads לזאת; the circulating transcription's לזות is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (25:28): הזהב] הזהוב AEF; וחנותו] ותנוהו ABEFG; החמשה] חמשה A.

verses.translation: To him who has{H3426}, it will be given{H5414}; and from him who has not{H369}, even what is due to him will be taken{H3947} from him.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew sharpens the hard saying: what is stripped from the empty-handed man is הראוי לו — 'what was DUE him,' his intended portion — where Greek has only 'even that which he hath.' Howard renders it 'that which was intended for him.' The idle servant does not merely lose his coin; he forfeits the share that was appointed his — the same word (ראוי) by which each man received 'as was fitting for him' in v. 15.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:29): תנתן] ינתן ABEF; לו ילקח] תלקח G.

verses.translation: And the lazy{H6102} servant{H5650} — cast him{H7993} into the dark places{H4285} of the depths{H8482}, and there{H8033} he will have weeping{H1065} and gnashing{H2786} of teeth{H8127}.

one_way_hebrew: במחשכי תחתיות — the two words stand together in Ps 88:7: 'Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, in dark places (בבור תחתיות במחשכים)'; cf. Lam 3:6 and Ps 143:3, 'he has made me sit in dark places (במחשכים) like the long dead.' The Hebrew names the servant's destination in the Psalter's own grave-language — a collocation no back-translation of 'outer darkness' would ever strike.
greek_deviations: Greek sends the servant to 'the outer darkness' (τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον) — darkness pictured as outside the banquet hall. The Hebrew sends him במחשכי תחתיות — 'into the dark places of the DEPTHS' — downward, not outward: the grave-darkness of the Psalms.
He is 'the LAZY servant' (העצל) to the end — Greek's 'unprofitable' (ἀχρεῖον) measures output; the Hebrew keeps the moral category of Proverbs it has used since v. 2.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:30): השליכהו] השליכוהו ABEFG; ושם] ששם EF; לו omitted in A.
The transcriber's footnote notes the defective spelling שנים for שינים ('teeth') here, as against 24:51.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: And when the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} comes{H935} in his appearance{H4758} with{H5973} his messengers{H4397}, then{H227} he will sit{H3427} on the throne{H3678} of his glory{H3519}.

one_way_hebrew: כסא כבודו — 'the throne of his glory': Jer 17:12 (כסא כבוד, 'a glorious high throne from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary') and 1 Sam 2:8. The enthronement scene is Dan 7:13-14 in Hebrew dress: the bar-enash comes, then sits.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew reads 'when the Son of Man comes במראהו — in his APPEARANCE — with his messengers,' where Greek has 'in his glory, and all the holy angels with him.' מראה is the seen form, Ezekiel's vision-word (Ezek 1:28, 'the appearance of the likeness of the glory of YHWH'); the Hebrew keeps כבוד ('glory') for the throne alone, and its messengers are neither 'all' nor 'holy' — simply his sent ones. Howard renders 'in his revelation.'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ק״ו (Perek 106) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (25:31): ובבוא] בבא B.

verses.translation: And all{H3605} the nations{H1471} will be gathered{H622} before him{H6440}, and he will separate{H6504} between them{H996} as the shepherd{H7462} separates{H6504} the sheep{H3775} from the goats{H5795}.

one_way_hebrew: הכשבים — the base ms spells 'sheep' כשב, the Torah's own metathesized form (Lev 3:7; 17:3; Num 18:17), which mss BEF normalize to the common כבשים. No translator working back from Greek πρόβατα would reach for Leviticus's rarer spelling; a Hebrew hand raised on the Torah would.

The scene is Ezek 34: 'As for you, my flock... I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he-goats' (Ezek 34:17), the shepherd-judgment chapter whose vocabulary returns at v. 36 (see there).

ויפריד (H6504) — the same separation verb the Hebrew discourse used at 24:41 (the messengers 'separate the good from the evil') and 24:51 (the master 'separates' the false servant): three scenes, one verb, one judgment — a weave Greek breaks with ἀφορίζω/διχοτομέω.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:32): הכשבים] הכבשים BEF.

verses.translation: And he will set{H3322} the sheep{H3775} at his right{H3225} and the goats{H5795} at his left{H8040}.

one_way_hebrew: ויציג (H3322) — Jacob's shepherd-verb: 'and he set (ויצג) the flocks' (Gen 30:38); Greek στήσει is bare 'stand.' Right and left as blessing and its opposite run from Gen 48:13-19 (Ephraim under the right hand) through Eccl 10:2 ('a wise man's heart is at his right hand, but a fool's heart at his left').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:33): הכשבים] הכבשים BEF; ויציג] ויפריד EF, ישיג G (Howard marks G's reading with a query).

verses.translation: Then{H227} he will speak{H1696} to those at his right{H3225}: Come{H935}, blessed ones{H1288}, the blessed{H1288} of my Father{H1}, and inherit{H3423} for yourselves the kingdom{H4468} of the heavens{H8064} prepared{H3559} for you from the creation{H1254} of the world{H5769} until{H5704} now{H6258}.

one_way_hebrew: בואו ברוכי — Laban's greeting to Abraham's servant: 'Come in, thou blessed of YHWH (בוא ברוך יהוה)' (Gen 24:31). The King welcomes the righteous with the Torah's own formula of welcome.
וירשו (H3423) — the land-possession verb of Deuteronomy ('go in and possess the land'); the kingdom is entered as Israel entered its inheritance.
ממלכות (H4468) — the rarer biblical noun for kingship (Jer 26:1); the consonants also permit reading מן + מלכות. Either way the kingdom of the heavens is the estate.
greek_deviations: Three Hebrew surpluses in one sentence. The inheritance is named: 'the kingdom OF THE HEAVENS' (Greek: 'the kingdom' unqualified). The preparation runs 'from the creation of the world UNTIL NOW' (מבריאת העולם עד עתה) — the exact formula of 24:21 (מבראת העולם עד עתה) — where Greek stops at 'from the foundation of the world': the kingdom was not merely founded early, it has been in preparation the whole age through. And the verb is ברא-creation (Gen 1:1), not the Greek's architectural καταβολή ('foundation').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:34): לאשר] אשר B; ברוכי] של B; אבי] + שבשמים G ('my Father who is in heaven'); ממלכות] מלכות G; השמים] שמים ABEF; העולם] עולם G.

verses.translation: For I hungered{H7456} and you gave{H5414} me to eat{H398}; I thirsted{H6770} and you gave me to drink{H8354}; I was{H1961} a wayfarer{H732} and you took me in{H622};

one_way_hebrew: אורח — the 'wayfarer' of Nathan's parable (2 Sam 12:4, the traveler for whom the rich man would not take of his own flock) and of Jer 14:8, where YHWH himself asks why he should be 'as a wayfarer (כארח) that turns aside to tarry for a night.' Greek ξένος ('stranger') is status; אורח is a man on the road needing a roof tonight.

ותאספוני (H622) — 'you gathered me in': Ps 27:10, 'when my father and my mother forsake me, then YHWH will take me in (יאספני)'; Josh 20:4, the city of refuge 'shall take him in.' The King describes hospitality with Scripture's verb for taking in the abandoned.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:35): רעבתי] רעבתם B; צמאתי] צאמתי G; G also varies at ותאספוני.

verses.translation: naked{H6174} and you clothed me{H3847}; sick{H2470} and you visited me{H1239}; I was{H1961} in the prison-house{H5470} and you came{H935} to me{H413}.

one_way_hebrew: בית הסוהר — Joseph's prison, and only Joseph's: בית הסהר occurs in Scripture solely in Gen 39:20-23 and 40:3-5, the house where the rejected brother sat for crimes he did not commit until he rose to the throne. The King locates himself in Joseph's cell; Greek ἐν φυλακῇ is any jail. Verse 39 even spells it defectively (הסהר) exactly as Genesis does.

ותבקרוני (H1239, baqar) — Ezek 34:11-12: 'Behold, I myself will search for my sheep and seek them out (ובקרתים), as a shepherd seeks out (כבקרת) his flock.' In the very pericope built on Ezek 34's sheep-and-goats judgment (v. 32 = Ezek 34:17), the righteous are credited with the shepherd's own biqqur — they sought out the sick as YHWH seeks his scattered flock. Greek ἐπεσκέψασθε cannot carry the echo.
translation_notes: The scan reads הסוהר; the circulating transcription's הסוהת is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:36): G adds הייתי after חולה ('I was sick'); ותבואו אלי] ותבקרוני A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the righteous{H6662} will answer{H6030}: Our Master{H113}, when{H4970} did we see you{H7200} hungry{H7457} and satisfied you{H7646}, or thirsty{H6771} and gave you drink{H8248}?

one_way_hebrew: והשבענוך (H7646, sava) — 'and SATISFIED you': the verb of God's own table (Ps 107:9, 'he satisfies the longing soul'; Ps 145:16). Greek ἐθρέψαμεν ('fed') is maintenance; השביע is filling to satisfaction — the righteous unknowingly did for the King what the Psalms say God does for man.
translation_notes: מתו — evidently for מתי ('when'), as v. 44 spells it; Howard prints מתו without comment and translates 'when.'
צמנו — an anomalous form for 'thirsty' (ABEF read צמא); Howard renders '(thirsty)' in parentheses. The scan reads יענו; the circulating transcription's יעני is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:37): יענו] + לו ABEF; הצדיקים] + ויאמרו G; והשבענוך] ושבענוך G; צמנו] צמא ABEF; והשקתוך] והשקינוך ABEFG.

verses.translation: Or naked{H6174} and covered you{H3680}?

one_way_hebrew: ערום וכסיתוך — Isa 58:7 verbatim: 'when thou seest the NAKED, that thou COVER him (כי תראה ערם וכסיתו).' The King's checklist is Isaiah's chosen fast — bread to the hungry, the poor brought home, the naked covered — and this verse keeps Isaiah's own consonants (ראה... ערום... כסה). Greek περιεβάλομεν ('clothed') translates the deed and erases the citation.
greek_deviations: The righteous' reply is leaner than the Greek: Greek 25:38 asks about the stranger AND the naked; the Hebrew reply has no wayfarer-clause here — the wayfarer stood in the King's speech (v. 35) but the righteous' litany runs straight from drink to nakedness.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:38): Verse 38 is omitted in FG (a haplography easy among the repeated ־וך endings); וכסיתוך] וכסונוך AB, וכסינוך E.

verses.translation: Or sick{H2470} and visited you{H1239}, or in the prison-house{H5470} and came{H935} to you{H413}?

one_way_hebrew: בית הסהר — spelled defectively here exactly as in Gen 39:20-23, Joseph's prison (see v. 36). The righteous repeat the shepherd's verb too: ובקרנוך, 'we sought you out' (Ezek 34:11-12).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:39): Verse 39 is omitted in FG.

verses.translation: And the King{H4428} will answer{H6030} and say{H559} to them: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, that every{H3605} time{H6471} you did{H6213} it to one{H259} poor{H6041} man of one{H259} of these{H428} little ones{H6996}, it is as though you did{H6213} it to me.

one_way_hebrew: עני (H6041) — Scripture's poor man, whose cause is God's own: 'he judged the cause of the poor and needy... was not this to know me? says YHWH' (Jer 22:16); 'he that is gracious to the poor lends to YHWH' (Prov 19:17). The Hebrew verse states Prov 19:17 as royal fact: done to the ani, received by the King.
greek_deviations: Two readings recast the saying. The Hebrew base text adds עני — the deed is done 'to one POOR man of these little ones' — and it LACKS 'my brothers': Greek reads 'one of the least of these MY BRETHREN (τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου),' and mss BEF supply מאחי to match, but the base text stands without it (Howard prints '(my brothers)' in parentheses). In the Shem Tov text the King's solidarity is with the poor as such — the עני of the Torah's protections (Deut 15:11; 24:14-15) — not first with a defined brotherhood.
textual_notes: The scan reads מאחד; the second-mem reading is certain — the variant מאחי ('of my brothers') belongs to BEF only.
Howard's apparatus (25:40): שבכל] שכל EF; מאחד] מאחי BEF; for the stretch מאחד... כאלו G reads אחד מכל אלו כאלו.

verses.translation: And also{H1571} he will speak{H1696} to those at his left{H8040}: Depart{H5493} from me, cursed ones{H779}, and go{H935} into the everlasting{H5769} fire{H784}, in the place{H4725} prepared{H3559} for you with{H5973} the Satan{H7854} and his messengers{H4397};

one_way_hebrew: סורו ממני — Ps 6:9's cry verbatim (סורו ממני כל פעלי און, 'depart from me, all workers of iniquity') — the psalm-line Greek Matthew itself quotes at 7:23. Here the Hebrew judgment scene speaks it natively.
ארורים (H779) — the covenant participle of Deut 27's twelve curses (ארור...); the left hand hears the plural of Mount Ebal.
greek_deviations: THE FIRE WAS PREPARED FOR YOU. Greek reads 'the eternal fire prepared for the DEVIL and his angels' — the cursed enter lodgings made for another. The Hebrew reads במקום מוכן לכם עם השטן ומלאכיו — 'in the place prepared FOR YOU, with the Satan and his messengers.' The sentence mirrors v. 34 exactly: המוכן לכם there, מוכן לכם here — a kingdom prepared for you, a place prepared for you; each company receives its own prepared portion, and the Satan is company, not landlord. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads with the Greek ('prepared for Ha-Satan and his messengers'), so the Shem Tov reading is its own deliberate text, not a family accident.
translation_notes: The scan reads ארורים; the circulating transcription's ארירים is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:41): וגם] ואשר EF; ממני] + מרעם G (Howard marks the reading with a query); מוכן] המוכן G.

verses.translation: for I hungered{H7456} and you did not give{H5414} me to eat{H398}; I thirsted{H6770} and you did not give me drink{H8248};

one_way_hebrew: The indictment inverts Isa 58:7 and Ezek 34 clause by clause (see vv. 35-36, 38): what the righteous did with Scripture's own verbs, these left undone with the same verbs negated — ולא... ולא, the cadence of the covenant curses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:42): שרעבתי] שרעב היתי G; נתתם לי לאכול] שבעתם אותי G; for the closing לי G reads אותי וכו׳.

verses.translation: I was{H1961} a wayfarer{H732} and you did not take me in{H622}; naked{H6174} and you did not cover{H3680} me; sick{H2470} and in the prison-house{H1004} and you did not visit{H1239} me.

translation_notes: The base text reads ובבית — 'and in the house' — without הסוהר; mss ABEF supply הסוהר ('the prison-house'), and Howard's English writes '(prison).' The ellipsis is natural Hebrew after vv. 36 and 39 fixed which house is meant.
The scan reads חולה; the circulating transcription's הולה is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:43): Verse 43 is omitted in G (see v. 42); ובבית] + הסוהר ABEF; ערום ולא כסיתם אותי omitted in A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} they too{H1571} will answer{H6030} and say{H559} to him: When{H4970} did we see you{H7200}, our Master{H113}, hungry{H7457} or thirsty{H6771}, or a wayfarer{H732}, or naked{H6174}, or sick{H2470}, or in the prison-house{H5470}, and were not with you{H5973}, serving{H8334} you?

one_way_hebrew: משרתים (H8334, sharat) — the verb of priestly ministry (Exod 28:35, 'to minister in the holy place'; Deut 10:8). The condemned describe what they withheld as temple-service — and unwittingly concede the point: service to the King was on offer in every hungry man, and they declined the priesthood of it. Greek διηκονήσαμεν ('waited on') is table-language.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:44): או בבית] ובבית B; וחולה] או חולה ABEF; אדוננו] אדונינו B; A reads the opening words in the order אדוננו מתי ראינוך; עמך omitted in EF.
The transcriber's footnote notes that Howard's English closes the verse with a question mark though the printed Hebrew lacks one.

verses.translation: And he will answer{H6030} them and say{H559}: I say{H559} to you, that every{H3605} time{H6471} you did not do{H6213} this{H2063} to one{H259} poor{H6041} man of these{H428} little ones{H6996}, it is as though you did not do{H6213} it to me{H413}.

greek_deviations: Again 'one POOR man of these little ones' (לעני אחד) — the Hebrew names the poor on both sides of the verdict (vv. 40, 45), and again without 'my brothers.' And where Greek opens with 'Amen,' the Hebrew King no longer swears — the אמן of v. 40 sealed the blessing; the condemnation comes as plain speech.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:45): לעני אחד] A reads the words in the order אחד לעני.

verses.translation: And these{H428} will go{H1980} to everlasting{H5769} abhorrence{H1860}, and the righteous{H6662} to everlasting{H5769} life{H2416}.

one_way_hebrew: THE VERSE IS DAN 12:2. Daniel: 'many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life (לחיי עולם), and some to shame and everlasting abhorrence (לדראון עולם).' The Shem Tov verse ends the discourse with BOTH of Daniel's destinies in Daniel's own consonants — דראון עולם and חיי עולם. The word דראון occurs in all of Scripture only in Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24 (the carcasses 'an abhorrence to all flesh'). Greek Matthew reads κόλασιν αἰώνιον, 'everlasting punishment' — a translation that loses the source; no back-translator from κόλασις would recover דראון. The discourse that began from Daniel's abomination (24:15) closes on Daniel's resurrection verse.
greek_deviations: Greek 'punishment' (κόλασις) states an infliction; דראון states a condition — to be an object of abhorrence, as Isa 66:24's rebels are to those who look on them. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'the fire of Gei-Hinnom... everlasting light' here; the Shem Tov text stands on Dan 12:2 exactly.
translation_notes: The scan reads לחיי; the circulating transcription's להיי is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (25:46): after the first עולם A adds עהב (evidently עה״ב, 'the world to come') and F adds ולנצח נצחים ('and for ever and ever').

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 25 in the Shem Tov Hebrew rewrites the hinges of all three judgment parables. (1) 25:1 — the virgins go out 'to meet a bridegroom AND A BRIDE' (לקראת חתן וכלה): the bride, absent from the standard Greek text (a few Western-Syriac witnesses preserve her), stands in every Shem Tov ms without recorded variant, and in the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew as well; with v. 10's chuppah (Greek: 'wedding feast') the parable carries all three wedding words of Joel 2:16 — bridegroom, bride, chuppah. (2) The gate: the wise enter and 'the GATE was shut' (השער, v. 10), the foolish call 'at the gate' (v. 11) — the same gates where 24:33 set the returning one; Greek has a house door. (3) 25:13 — 'you do not know the day and the hour WHEN THE BRIDEGROOM COMES,' keeping the warning inside the parable where the Greek trails off. (4) 25:2's 'lazy fools' (עצלות כסילות) plants Proverbs' sluggard-word that returns as the verdict on the buried-money servant (vv. 26, 30) — one moral thread the Greek lacks in both places; likewise the foolish lamps 'go out' (נדעכו, v. 8) with the verb Scripture reserves for the lamp of the wicked (Prov 13:9). (5) 25:17, 28 — the two-piece servant 'gained five others' like his fellow, and the coin goes 'to the one who GAINED the five' (Greek: 'gained two'; 'him who has ten'): reward tracks faithfulness, not holdings, and the identical greetings of vv. 21/23 say the same. (6) 25:30 — the lazy servant is cast 'into the dark places of the depths' (במחשכי תחתיות), Ps 88:7's grave-darkness, where Greek has 'outer darkness.' (7) 25:31 — the Son of Man comes 'in his appearance (במראהו) with his messengers' — no 'glory,' no 'holy angels'; glory belongs to the throne. (8) 25:34 — 'inherit the kingdom OF THE HEAVENS prepared for you from the creation of the world UNTIL NOW' — the formula of 24:21 repeated. (9) 25:40, 45 — the deed is done 'to one POOR man (עני) of these little ones,' and the base text lacks 'my brothers' (mss BEF supply מאחי after the Greek): the King's solidarity is with the poor as such (Prov 19:17). (10) 25:41 — the everlasting fire is 'in the place prepared FOR YOU with the Satan and his messengers' — mirroring v. 34's 'prepared for you' — where Greek makes the fire the devil's estate; Vat. Ebr. 100 sides with the Greek, isolating the Shem Tov reading as deliberate. (11) 25:46 — the discourse ends in Dan 12:2's own consonants: 'everlasting abhorrence' (דראון עולם) and 'everlasting life' (חיי עולם); Greek's 'everlasting punishment' erases the citation. One-way Hebrew throughout: Exod 12:29/Ruth 3:8 at v. 6 (ויהי בחצי הלילה), Exod 30:7's lamp-dressing at v. 7, Gen 24:31's 'come, blessed' at v. 34, Joseph's בית הסהר (Gen 39:20) at vv. 36/39, Ezek 34's shepherd who 'seeks out' (בקר) at vv. 32-39, Isa 58:7 verbatim at v. 38, Ps 6:9 at v. 41, and the כון-thread (ready/prepared: 24:44; 25:10, 34, 41). Shem Tov's own section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 104), 14 (105), and 31 (106). Mss FG omit vv. 38-39; G omits v. 43; F omits v. 23.
